## Highlights

Zova 1.4.0 makes large objects and database maintenance practical at scale.
Object writes, reads and deletes are much faster, a new seekable reader serves
HTTP range requests without re-hashing whole chunks, and deleted data can be
returned to the filesystem in place. Long backups, compactions and migrations
now report progress and can be cancelled. Storage moves to format 13, so
databases written by 1.3.0 need one explicit `zova migrate` before 1.4.0 opens
them.

## What's changed

### Objects

- Faster `ObjectWriter` ingest. Chunks are hashed once, inserted in batches
  and committed every 64 MiB instead of once per write call, and `finish` no
  longer re-reads or re-hashes stored chunks. A 32 MiB FastCDC object written
  in 1 MiB calls went from about 2.6 s to about 0.3 s in a local probe.
- Object and chunk hashing picks hardware SHA-256 (ARMv8 SHA-2 or x86 SHA-NI)
  at run time. The Rust, Python, JavaScript and Go packages, which are built
  from generated C, previously always used portable rounds; on Apple M1 the
  hash runs about 10x faster. Digests are unchanged.
- Full-object reads hash each byte once, and FastCDC range reads find their
  first chunk by binary search instead of walking the whole manifest.
- Deleting objects no longer scans every manifest row. A new chunk-reference
  index makes deleting a 64 MiB FastCDC object from a store with 1M manifest
  rows take 0.11 s instead of about 12 minutes.
- Added a seekable, verified object reader for range serving:
  `Database.objectSeekableReader` in Zig and
  `zova_object_seekable_reader_create`/`_read`/`_seek`/`_destroy` in the C ABI.
  It loads one chunk at a time, checks its SHA-256 once, and serves later reads
  in that chunk from memory. It is exposed as an `io.ReadSeeker` in Go,
  `Read + Seek` readers in Rust, a file-like object in Python, and sync and
  async readers in JavaScript.
- Fixed a crash when `ObjectReader` failed to load its first chunk: the
  manifest statement was finalized twice instead of returning `ObjectCorrupt`.

### Reclaiming disk space

- New databases, split stores and `zova compact` output use SQLite
  incremental auto-vacuum. `zova reclaim [--json] [--max-pages <n>]`,
  `Database.reclaimSpace` and `zova_database_reclaim` release free pages back
  to the filesystem in bounded steps, without rewriting the database.
- The bindings expose it as `reclaim_space` (Rust and Python), `ReclaimSpace`
  (Go) and `reclaimSpace` (JavaScript, sync and async).
- Migrate, backup, restore and convert keep the source file's auto-vacuum
  mode. Files created before 1.4.0 keep reclaiming space through
  `zova compact`; `zova reclaim` points them there.

### Maintenance

- Backup, compact and migrate report progress through an optional callback,
  in Zig and through `zova_database_backup_with_progress`,
  `zova_database_compact_with_progress` and
  `zova_database_migrate_with_progress`. Every binding accepts a progress
  callback; returning non-zero, raising, or aborting cancels the operation,
  which fails with the new `ZOVA_INTERRUPTED` status and publishes nothing.
- The CLI shows a live progress line on a terminal, `--progress` prints plain
  progress lines, and `--json --progress` writes line-delimited JSON events to
  stderr.
- `zova migrate --dry-run` reports the planned files, page and byte counts,
  free space at the destination, and whether every installed extension is
  available, without creating or changing anything.
- The Rust, Go, Python and JavaScript bindings can migrate a database that has
  non-bundled extensions installed, using the same bundle paths and trust
  store as their open calls.
- Copy verification during backup, compact, restore, migrate and split streams
  each object through a fixed buffer. Peak memory for a backup holding a
  512 MiB object dropped from about 551 MB to about 12 MB.
- Fixed copy verification rejecting every database that held a
  streaming-profile object (fixed 1 MiB chunks) as corrupt.

### Graphs

- Keyed graph puts of up to 256 distinct keys resolve existing nodes and edges
  with point lookups instead of reading the whole graph, so small batches into
  a large graph no longer cost time proportional to the graph.

## Compatibility

- Package and C ABI identity are `1.4.0`. The C ABI change is additive; code
  built against 1.3.0 keeps working. Code that switches over every
  `zova_status` value should handle the new `ZOVA_INTERRUPTED` (18).
- Storage format is now 13. Open never migrates silently: format 9, 10, 11 and
  12 databases are reported as migration-required and left unchanged. Migrate
  them with `zova migrate` or the `migrate` call in any binding. Zova 1.3.0 and
  earlier cannot open format-13 files, and downgrades are unsupported.
- The plugin ABI stays at v1. No new plugin operations were added.
- Existing 1.x ownership, ordering, error, and transaction guarantees remain in
  force.

## Installation and distribution

- Native packages use `1.4.0` across Cargo, PyPI, npm, and Go.
- Python publishes CPython 3.13 stable-ABI wheels tested on Python 3.13 and
  3.14; no Python source distribution is published.
- npm publishes `zova-js`, its native companion packages, and the experimental
  `zova-wasm` package.
- Go's module tag is `bindings/go/v1.4.0`.

## Known boundaries

On macOS, the first large write into a nearly empty incremental-mode file can
take longer to commit, because SQLite rewrites an early bookkeeping page during
the write and macOS then flushes the pending data at commit. Measured cost
ranged from about 5% on an internal disk to about 60–75% on an external disk.
Once a file holds data, the cost is the same as without auto-vacuum. A seekable or partial range
read verifies each chunk it returns, not the whole-object hash. Linked plugin
descriptors are available through the C ABI and Zig only. Core vector search
remains exact; approximate search is available only through the experimental
USearch reference extension. Extension authoring beyond the documented common
C ABI, the reference extensions, and the separate browser WASM API remain
experimental and outside the stable native 1.x compatibility commitment.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/ata-sesli/zova/compare/v1.3.0...v1.4.0
